question.text: Two cars <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> are approaching each other with velocities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>72</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively. The frequency of a whistle sound as emitted by a passenger in car <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo></math> heard by the passenger in car <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1320</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the velocity of sound in air is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>340</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>ms</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> the actual frequency of the whistle sound produced is ________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
